local_only.title: Local pseudopotentials accelerate neural network wavefunction simulations

official_catalog_articles.summary: A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.
official_catalog_articles.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection

official_catalog_articles.summary: We discuss the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematical research and explore its implications for the computational science community.
official_catalog_articles.title: The rise of AI in mathematics — and science

official_catalog_articles.summary: The study shows that guiding AI agents with descriptions of how people make decisions in a supply-chain game helps agents reproduce collective human behavior.
official_catalog_articles.title: Cognitive grounding improves LLM simulation of collective human behavior

official_catalog_articles.summary: By training a reservoir computing system without access to its intermediate states and by eliminating the coupling between its nodes, a physical learning framework achieves efficient learning both in simulation and on optoelectronic hardware.
official_catalog_articles.title: Training reservoirs without looking back
Open foundation models for clinical AI

official_catalog_articles.summary: Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.
official_catalog_articles.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study presents a scalable, efficient framework for unconventional computing with physical neural networks. It replaces dense connections with uncoupled one-dimensional dynamics, simplifies training, improves performance and reduces resource use.
official_catalog_articles.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture

official_catalog_articles.summary: Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.
official_catalog_articles.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction

official_catalog_articles.summary: Author-proposed non-primary articles can bring fresh and timely perspectives to the journal. Here, we discuss the factors that editors consider when assessing proposals for these contributions.
official_catalog_articles.title: Making the case for a non-primary article

official_catalog_articles.summary: Structure coefficients provide a unified way to identify dynamic network structures that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.
official_catalog_articles.title: Dynamic networks can promote pro-sociality

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.
official_catalog_articles.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks

official_catalog_articles.summary: An automated framework, HDOCK-Multimer (HDM), is developed that integrates ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly for the structure prediction of large protein complexes. Across three benchmarks, HDM demonstrates increased accuracy and robustness in modeling large protein assemblies, compared with state-of-the-art assembly and deep learning-based methods.
official_catalog_articles.title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
official_catalog_articles.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly

official_catalog_articles.summary: Accurately predicting properties of materials is one of the main challenges in computational materials science. Systematic experiments now show that large language models (LLMs) struggle to use positional information for the prediction of those properties. This limitation does not reverse as model or dataset sizes grow.
official_catalog_articles.title: LLMs predict material properties based on atom types and not atom positions

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors introduce an extension of machine learning interatomic potentials that predicts molecular Hessians directly, improving accuracy and speed compared in transition-state searches, geometry optimization and vibrational analysis relative to Hessians from automatic differentiation.
official_catalog_articles.title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives

official_catalog_articles.summary: Researchers show that large language models cannot learn from spatial coordinates regardless of model or data scale. Specialized geometric neural networks consistently outperform language models for material property prediction.
official_catalog_articles.title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models

official_catalog_articles.summary: A physics-based in situ learning method is demonstrated that directly measures optical gradients with photonic integrated circuits, allowing diverse circuit topologies to be trained after fabrication. This hardware achieves matrix design, multiwavelength computation and rapid meta-learning without requiring a full digital model of the circuit.
official_catalog_articles.title: Photonic circuits become trainable AI hardware

official_catalog_articles.summary: A recent study reports a property-first computational strategy, identifying coordinated parameter changes that can tune several features of a complex oscillator at the same time.
official_catalog_articles.title: Steering complex rhythms

official_catalog_articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is enabling epidemic models to learn across outbreaks. The next challenge is ensuring that these models learn and transfer not mere statistical patterns, but epidemiological mechanisms.
official_catalog_articles.title: Epidemiological modeling in the age of artificial intelligence

official_catalog_articles.summary: Researchers pair active learning with geometric deep learning to predict the outcome and site selectivity of chemical reactions from scarce data, guiding experiments that accelerate drug discovery and expand accessible chemical space.
official_catalog_articles.title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study reports a physics-based in situ learning method that trains artificial neural networks directly within the photonic integrated circuits, turning diverse optical circuits into efficient AI learning hardware.
official_catalog_articles.title: Photonic neuromorphic learning via generalized in situ physical gradient descent

official_catalog_articles.summary: CellART is a deep learning framework that recovers individual cells from high-resolution spatial transcriptomics data, predicting cell boundaries and cell types together across different platforms and tissue types.
official_catalog_articles.title: CellART: a unified framework for extracting single-cell information from high-resolution spatial transcriptomics

official_catalog_articles.summary: This Article reports a property-based framework with a rigorous mathematical foundation for modulating complex rhythms. It identifies the fewest parameters for producing desired spatiotemporal behaviors, and is validated in oscillatory networks and engineered circuits.
official_catalog_articles.title: Modulatability of complex oscillators

official_catalog_articles.summary: A machine learning-based algorithm is proposed for exploring unknown parts of chemical space.
official_catalog_articles.title: Towards a chemistry genome

official_catalog_articles.summary: The challenge of understanding cortical folding is compounded by data limitations. A recent physics-transfer learning framework bridges the gap between simple mechanical models and complex brain geometries, allowing for better predictions of brain morphogenesis.
official_catalog_articles.title: Learning brain folds from simpler shapes

official_catalog_articles.summary: A collaborative system of large language model agents brings protein engineering closer to natural-language interaction, lowering the barrier between human intent and biomolecular design.
official_catalog_articles.title: Intuitive enzyme design with LLM agents

official_catalog_articles.summary: Embodied intelligence has enabled machines to act autonomously, yet intelligence remains largely confined to digital models, leaving robotic bodies as passive executors. In extreme environments, such as the human brain, where tissues are mechanically and thermally sensitive, conventional electronics can become limiting. Here, we discuss how active materials, which embed intelligence directly within their structure, can expand robotic capabilities in these settings, with a particular focus on the role of computation-aided design.
official_catalog_articles.title: Computational active materials and embodied intelligence in extreme conditions

official_catalog_articles.summary: Reproducibility has long been a concern in machine learning research. The rise of large language models adds new layers of complexity, underscoring the need for clearer reporting standards and community-wide best practices.
official_catalog_articles.title: Reproducibility in the era of large language models

official_catalog_articles.summary: While there are widespread concerns about the potential negative societal impacts of algorithm-driven systems, a more balanced approach to understanding online content consumption and engagement that considers both algorithmic mechanisms and human agency will be crucial moving forward.
official_catalog_articles.title: Algorithmic systems, human agency and the future of platform research

official_catalog_articles.summary: Large language models can potentially serve as human proxies across various roles, enabling nuanced simulations of behavior. This Review categorizes their applications, stressing distinct evaluation methods and validity criteria essential for accurate scientific claims and practical implementations.
official_catalog_articles.title: Large language models as human proxies

official_catalog_articles.summary: A descriptor, TDiMS, is developed to summarize the enumerated pairwise topological distances between molecular substructures and identify interpretable molecular features for materials discovery.
official_catalog_articles.title: Revisiting molecular descriptors with TDiMS for interpretable intramolecular interactions based on substructure pairs

official_catalog_articles.summary: By integrating intracranial neural signals from gray and white matter, we developed personalized deep learning models that accurately decoded continuous valence and arousal states across image and video viewing tasks. The models generalized across tasks, revealed emotion-encoding brain subnetworks and enabled low-latency real-time decoding, bringing affective brain–computer interfaces closer to being suitable for closed-loop therapy.
official_catalog_articles.title: Deep learning models enable high-performance, real-time emotion decoding from intracranial brain activity

official_catalog_articles.summary: A natural-language-guided pathology segmentation model is developed to link pathological language with pathology image content to produce semantic masks, offering a path toward computational pathology systems that are more flexible, interpretable and aligned with human expertise.
official_catalog_articles.title: When pathology segmentation learns to listen

official_catalog_articles.summary: MutexaGPT turns plain-language enzyme-engineering intuitions into lead mutation designs through AI agent-orchestrated high-throughput molecular modeling, yielding experimentally validated improvements in enzyme specificity and cold activity.
official_catalog_articles.title: MutexaGPT: an intuition-to-design translator for physics-based enzyme engineering

official_catalog_articles.summary: This Resource introduces PathSegmentor—a foundation model that segments 160 pathological categories via natural language prompts, generalizes across datasets and clinical cohorts, and enables scalable, interpretable pathology image analysis.
official_catalog_articles.title: Segment anything in pathology images with natural language

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors develop a physics-transfer learning framework that learns cortical folding physics from simple geometries and transfers it to complex brain structures, enabling accurate prediction of brain morphogenesis from limited data.
official_catalog_articles.title: Predicting brain morphogenesis via physics-transfer learning

official_catalog_articles.summary: A large-scale experiment at a major machine learning conference shows that when researchers privately rank their own submissions, those rankings forecast future citations more reliably than peer-review scores.
official_catalog_articles.title: When authors are the best judges of their work
AI testing is not AI safety
Publisher Correction: Continual integration of single-cell multimodal data with MIRACLE

official_catalog_articles.summary: Most patients leave the clinic with only a few of the clinical measurements needed to tell the full story of their health. PULSE is a new artificial intelligence (AI) framework that fills in the blanks, using a patient’s own history to predict what was never directly measured.
official_catalog_articles.title: A patient’s longitudinal history reconstructs their unmeasured molecular profile

official_catalog_articles.summary: PULSE is an AI framework that uses patients’ longitudinal electronic health records to accurately generate within- and cross-modal data from routine clinical laboratory tests, enabling cost-effective precision medicine across diverse biomedical settings.
official_catalog_articles.title: Longitudinal alignments and syntheses of multimodal clinical data for personalized medicine with the PULSE framework

official_catalog_articles.summary: This work presents an efficient and modular framework called CrysVCD, which integrates chemical rules directly into the generative process for valence-constrained design.
official_catalog_articles.title: Enhancing materials discovery with valence-constrained design in generative modeling

official_catalog_articles.summary: The study finds that authors’ rankings of their own AI conference papers predict later citations better than peer-review scores, suggesting that self-rankings could provide a simple complement to peer review.
official_catalog_articles.title: Self-rankings as a predictor of scientific impact beyond peer review

official_catalog_articles.summary: As AI becomes increasingly embedded in research and scientific publishing, transparency, accountability, and human oversight remain essential to safeguarding research integrity.
official_catalog_articles.title: Responsible and transparent use of AI in scientific publishing

official_catalog_articles.summary: As large language models begin to plan and run experiments on their own, the reflex is to demand that they be interpretable before they are trusted. We argue that what grounds trust in autonomous science is not a view inside the model; it is provenance: a complete, re-openable record of what was reasoned, done and measured that can be audited and set right when it is wrong, making autonomy a corrective for the literature’s biases rather than a threat to rigor. Interpretability remains valuable, but the record is the gateway to trust.
official_catalog_articles.title: Provenance grounds trust in autonomous science

official_catalog_articles.summary: Addressing generalization limits in machine learning models for chemical reactions, this work introduces a pretraining scheme that enables accurate predictions for unseen chemistry and expands computational discovery.
official_catalog_articles.title: Robust generative transition-state models for unseen chemistry

official_catalog_articles.summary: A universal generative model — InfoMetaGen — provides an inverse design strategy for subwavelength meta-atoms and inhomogeneous metamaterial distributions.
official_catalog_articles.title: A universal metamaterial generative model

official_catalog_articles.summary: A newly generated high-throughput experimentation (HTE) dataset is integrated with open-source data to produce a large and high-quality Buchwald–Hartwig reaction dataset for training machine learning models. The combination of HTE and active learning enabled the development of a robust machine-learning model with reliable out-of-distribution predictive power.
official_catalog_articles.title: Model-guided data production unlocks reliable reaction predictions

official_catalog_articles.summary: A predictive model capable of generalizing to previously unseen Buchwald–Hartwig chemical space is built to enable rapid, in silico optimization, reducing reaction scouting time from weeks to minutes.
official_catalog_articles.title: Robust out-of-distribution prediction of Buchwald–Hartwig reactions

official_catalog_articles.summary: An empirical scaling advantage for solving representative NP-complete problems is demonstrated by integrating a restricting space reduction algorithm with quantum solvers. Consequently, quantum resources are shown to grow more slowly than classical counterparts.
official_catalog_articles.title: Quantum scaling advantage using reduced search in an NP-complete problem

official_catalog_articles.summary: MIRACLE is an online continual learning framework that efficiently integrates single-cell multimodal data across batches, modalities, tissues, and diseases.
official_catalog_articles.title: Continual integration of single-cell multimodal data with MIRACLE

official_catalog_articles.summary: A new method designs RNA sequences by learning from alignments of structurally similar molecules, producing aptamers and ribozymes that are experimentally validated.
official_catalog_articles.title: Structural alignments to design functional RNAs

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study presents AlignIF, which uses multiple structure alignments to capture evolutionary rules and conservation patterns across RNA families, enabling diverse, structure-guided designs of functional aptamers and ribozymes.
official_catalog_articles.title: Structure-alignment-driven cross-graph modeling for functional RNA design

official_catalog_articles.summary: SpatialFormer, a transformer-based model for spatial transcriptomics, learns cell–cell relationships to predict cell co-localization, annotate cell types and niches, and reveal cell communication gene pairs in pulmonary fibrosis.
official_catalog_articles.title: SpatialFormer: universal spatial representation learning from subcellular molecular to multicellular landscapes

official_catalog_articles.summary: Privacy, utility, and efficiency benchmarks have advanced privacy-preserving genome-wide association studies (GWAS) but often fall short of supporting organizational decisions about responsible data sharing. Future benchmarks should connect formal guarantees and assumptions to institutional risk, accountability, and decision making.
official_catalog_articles.title: Rethinking privacy-preserving GWAS benchmarks for governance

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study reports personalized models that decode human emotion states from intracranial brain recordings in real time, work across different tasks and uncover key brain networks that could guide future treatments for mental health conditions.
official_catalog_articles.title: Cross-task, explainable and real-time decoding of human emotion states by integrating gray and white matter intracranial neural activity

official_catalog_articles.summary: We present DIPPER (distance-based phylogenetic placer), a graphics processing unit-accelerated computational tool for reconstruction of evolutionary trees from genome sequences. By combining a divide-and-conquer strategy with highly parallel, memory-efficient distance computation, DIPPER scales to ten million sequences (1–2 orders of magnitude beyond the limits of existing tools) while improving both speed and memory efficiency.
official_catalog_articles.title: Fast reconstruction of evolutionary trees from millions of genome sequences

official_catalog_articles.summary: We highlight how AlphaFold2 has advanced protein design and inspired the development of artificial intelligence-driven infrastructures for scientific discovery.
official_catalog_articles.title: AlphaFold2 turns five

official_catalog_articles.summary: A generative model designs information metamaterials from meta-atoms to programmable arrays, enabling beam steering, focusing and holography with experimental validation and more than 1,000-fold faster holographic design.
official_catalog_articles.title: Generative model for information metamaterial design

official_catalog_articles.summary: Universal machine learning force fields excel on computational benchmarks but consistently fail when tested against experimental measurements of real minerals, underscoring the need for evaluation frameworks grounded in real-world conditions and multiple material properties beyond energy and forces.
official_catalog_articles.title: UniFFBench: evaluating universal machine learning force fields against experimental measurements

official_catalog_articles.summary: Protein language models are powerful computational tools for protein fitness prediction. The recent investigation into the relationship between model outputs and prediction accuracy reveals the scaling behavior of such models and provides practical guidelines for their applications to fitness prediction.
official_catalog_articles.title: Protein fitness prediction with language models

official_catalog_articles.summary: Larger language models do not always perform better at fitness prediction. Hou et al. found that performance depends on whether model outputs match evolutionary patterns in homologs, which is best achieved at moderate predicted sequence likelihoods.
official_catalog_articles.title: Understanding language model scaling for protein fitness prediction

official_catalog_articles.summary: A diffusion-based multimodal framework called DISSECT leverages transcriptomic gradients to refine segmentation boundaries, enabling high-precision single-cell segmentation even in densely packed regions.
official_catalog_articles.title: Spatial transcriptome for cell segmentation

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study shows that local pseudopotentials boost the efficiency of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo while preserving accuracy, enabling reliable simulations of large, challenging iron–sulfur clusters.
official_catalog_articles.title: Empowering neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo with local pseudopotentials

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors propose a framework that integrates cytological imaging and spatial transcriptomics to improve cell segmentation and enable reconstruction of spatial single-cell transcriptomes.
official_catalog_articles.title: Integrating cytological images and spatial transcriptomics for cell segmentation with DISSECT

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study introduces DIPPER, a GPU-accelerated tool that efficiently reconstructs evolutionary trees from tens of millions of genome sequences, extending scalability by one to two orders of magnitude beyond that of existing tools.
official_catalog_articles.title: Ultrafast and ultralarge distance-based phylogenetics using DIPPER

official_catalog_articles.summary: The researchers developed NEP89, a foundation model for large-scale molecular dynamics across 89 elements with near-quantum-level accuracy and high efficiency. It can be rapidly adapted to address complex challenges in inorganic and organic materials.
official_catalog_articles.title: NEP89: universal neuroevolution potential for inorganic and organic materials across 89 elements

official_catalog_articles.summary: Organoid intelligence represents a new frontier for computing inspired by the human brain. This Review discusses the evolution of brain-inspired computing along with potential challenges for future development.
official_catalog_articles.title: Computing inspired by the brain: a journey from algorithms to organoids

official_catalog_articles.summary: HUMID is a bottom-up coarse-grained framework for proton transport that bridges the quantum and molecular scales, enabling simulations of reactive transport dynamics across diverse environments with over 1,000-fold greater computational efficiency.
official_catalog_articles.title: Systematic bottom-up coarse-graining of hydrated excess proton transport across scales

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study introduces RF-PHATE, a supervised visualization method that preserves data structure while revealing biological patterns, enabling insights into disease progression in multiple sclerosis, COVID-19 and other biological contexts.
official_catalog_articles.title: Gaining biological insights through supervised data visualization

official_catalog_articles.summary: Geographical disparities regarding the availability of GPU hardware are becoming a structural constraint on scientific participation itself and must be addressed.
official_catalog_articles.title: The inequalities of GPU access

official_catalog_articles.summary: Although social technologies are increasingly co-shaping the public sphere, these systems were not designed as democratic infrastructure. Here, we propose a framework for societal alignment that focuses on procedural fairness to mitigate urgent risks and align emerging technology with societal values.
official_catalog_articles.title: Social technologies need societal alignment

official_catalog_articles.summary: A new library of combinatorial optimization problems provides a standardized testing ground to rigorously compare quantum and classical algorithms, paving the way for demonstrating quantum utility.
official_catalog_articles.title: Setting benchmarks for practical quantum utility of combinatorial optimization

official_catalog_articles.summary: This Resource presents the Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library, which enables fair, reproducible benchmarks of quantum heuristics for ten difficult combinatorial optimization classes with baseline results to track progress towards quantum advantage.
official_catalog_articles.title: The Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study develops enhanced quantum solvers for an NP-complete Boolean satisfiability problem and reports empirical scaling advantages over leading classical solvers in large-scale simulations, with supporting validation on a superconducting quantum processor.
official_catalog_articles.title: Evidence of scaling advantage on an NP-complete problem with enhanced quantum solvers

official_catalog_articles.summary: A gene–environment interaction test (SAGELD) is developed to speed up large-scale genome-wide analyses using longitudinal data, facilitating novel discoveries on genetic variants that modify the effects of environmental exposures.
official_catalog_articles.title: Testing longitudinal gene–environment interactions

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors introduce SAGELD, a method that leverages longitudinal data to detect gene–environment interactions with greater statistical power than conventional approaches based on cross-sectional data, improving discovery in large biobank studies.
official_catalog_articles.title: Leveraging longitudinal data to boost statistical power for gene–environment interaction analysis

official_catalog_articles.summary: Understanding how people move through cities is essential for public health and urban planning, yet most cities worldwide lack reliable mobility data. A new model reconstructs these movement patterns from openly available maps and population data, revealing that income inequality shapes urban mobility in ways that transcend local geography.
official_catalog_articles.title: Reconstructing urban mobility from the built environment

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study presents neuroGravity—a model that merges physics with machine learning to reconstruct mobility networks in data-scarce regions. It provides crucial tools for equitable urban planning, revealing income segregation as a core determinant of human flows.
official_catalog_articles.title: Transferable human mobility network reconstruction with neuroGravity

official_catalog_articles.summary: MetaSTAARlite provides a scalable and resource-efficient summary statistics-based pipeline for powerful, functionally informed rare-variant meta-analysis of biobank-scale sequencing data.
official_catalog_articles.title: MetaSTAARlite: an all-in-one tool for biobank-scale whole-genome sequencing meta-analysis

official_catalog_articles.summary: MetaSTAARlite provides a scalable and resource-efficient summary statistics-based pipeline for powerful, functionally informed rare-variant meta-analysis of biobank-scale sequencing data.
official_catalog_articles.title: MetaSTAARlite: an all-in-one tool for biobank-scale whole-genome sequencing meta-analysis

official_catalog_articles.summary: We developed FLOWR, a structure-aware multi-purpose generative model unifying de novo ligand generation, fragment-based and interaction-conditional sampling. We demonstrated that FLOWR generates ligands up to 70-fold faster compared with existing methods while improving the physical validity and interaction accuracy of generated compounds.
official_catalog_articles.title: Flow matching for fast, multi-purpose structure-based ligand generation for drug discovery

official_catalog_articles.summary: The Open Materials 2024 dataset provides a large-scale, open-access collection of quantum-chemical atomistic simulations that encompasses diverse off-equilibrium crystal structures, thereby making machine-learning interatomic potentials more robust across different materials prediction tasks.
official_catalog_articles.title: Elevating universal interatomic potentials with large-scale off-equilibrium data

official_catalog_articles.summary: This Resource introduces the Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) dataset, offering more than 110 million diverse density functional theory calculations. AI models trained on OMat24 achieve a high accuracy and can eliminate systematic biases across model architectures.
official_catalog_articles.title: The Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) inorganic materials dataset and models

official_catalog_articles.summary: Nature Computational Science now takes part in the co-review initiative in order to encourage the involvement of early-career researchers in the peer review process and to ensure proper recognition of their service.
official_catalog_articles.title: Supporting early-career researchers in peer review

official_catalog_articles.summary: Protein language models can effectively decode evolution’s grammar, making structure prediction and design scalable. This transformative capability is accelerating biological discovery and engineering across all scales.
official_catalog_articles.title: Protein language models for structural biology

official_catalog_articles.summary: FLOWR combines continuous and categorical flow matching with equivariant optimal transport and a separate protein pocket encoder to improve validity, pose accuracy and interaction recovery at substantially faster inference speeds.
official_catalog_articles.title: FLOWR: flow matching for structure-aware de novo, interaction- and fragment-based ligand generation

official_catalog_articles.summary: This Perspective explores the extent to which AI democratizes knowledge work and discusses potential intervention strategies for addressing social and place-based divides.
official_catalog_articles.title: AI and the democratization of knowledge work

official_catalog_articles.summary: A framework called HELIX provides a strategy for predicting full-length transcript isoform usage across diverse biological contexts by integrating sequence features with RNA-binding protein expression.
official_catalog_articles.title: Modeling context-dependent RNA splicing by deep learning

official_catalog_articles.summary: HELIX is a deep learning framework for modeling tissue- and context-specific RNA splicing and isoform usage, prioritizing splicing-altering genetic variants and their functional effects from bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data.
official_catalog_articles.title: HELIX: a scalable model for predicting context-dependent regulation of RNA splicing and isoform usage

official_catalog_articles.summary: This work reports HESpotEx, an artificial intelligence model that predicts spot-level spatial gene expression from whole-slide histopathology images to capture the tissue molecular patterns across cancers and inflammatory diseases.
official_catalog_articles.title: HESpotEx: a dual-stream deep learning framework for spot-level gene expression prediction from histological images

official_catalog_articles.summary: We developed a Geneformer model with an expanded pretraining dataset of more than 100 million single-cell human transcriptomes. The increased data diversity and model size improved downstream biological predictions in network biology. We implemented model quantization, which retained the model’s biological knowledge while significantly reducing GPU compute requirements, thereby improving model accessibility.
official_catalog_articles.title: Scaling and quantization of a foundational deep learning model for network biology

official_catalog_articles.summary: A general-purpose large language model can be trained to create a specialized model, SmileyLlama, that can generate drug-like molecules with user-specified properties that are relevant to medicinal chemistry through a process that might be extended to other scientific domains.
official_catalog_articles.title: SmileyLlama: modifying large language models for directed chemical space exploration

official_catalog_articles.summary: DeepSeMS, a transformer-based generative framework, translates biodiversity into chemical diversity by predicting microbial secondary metabolite structures directly from biosynthetic gene cluster sequences. Applied to global ocean metagenomes, Earth’s largest unexplored microbial reservoir, it uncovers novel molecular structures at scale and expands natural product candidates for drug discovery.
official_catalog_articles.title: Translating biodiversity into chemical diversity

official_catalog_articles.summary: This work presents DeepSeMS, a transformer-based framework that translates biosynthetic gene clusters into candidate secondary metabolite structures, enabling scalable exploration of chemical diversity from uncultivated global ocean microbiomes.
official_catalog_articles.title: DeepSeMS: revealing the hidden biosynthetic potential of the global ocean microbiome with a large language model

official_catalog_articles.summary: Gene regulatory networks provide a systems-level view of transcriptional control. Advances in biotechnology and computational modeling are reshaping gene regulatory network inference and opening up opportunities for mechanistic insight.
official_catalog_articles.title: The evolution of gene regulatory networks

official_catalog_articles.summary: We discuss common feedback from reviewers based on our experience as editors.
official_catalog_articles.title: What reviewers request the most

official_catalog_articles.summary: Engineering simulations traditionally rely on finite element methods, which are accurate but computationally expensive, while scientific machine learning offers faster, data-driven alternatives. The recently developed neural-operator element method combines both approaches, making simulations more efficient and scalable.
official_catalog_articles.title: Merging the classical and the modern in physics-based simulations

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors propose a method that unifies finite element methods and machine learning by using neural operators as elements to model complex subdomains, yielding an efficient and scalable numerical framework with highly reusable machine learning models.
official_catalog_articles.title: NOEM: efficient and scalable finite element method enabled by reusable neural operators

official_catalog_articles.summary: Sustainable development faces challenges from the complexities across environmental, social and economic systems. This Review discusses advances in understanding collective dynamics in infrastructure systems—focusing on energy and mobility—highlighting the need for interdisciplinary, data-driven tools.
official_catalog_articles.title: Sustainability as a challenge in complex systems dynamics

official_catalog_articles.summary: We introduce DualGPT-AB, a dual-stage conditional generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) framework for therapeutic antibody design that simultaneously optimizes antigen-binding specificity and developabilities. DualGPT-AB facilitates efficient antibody sequence generation, producing candidates with enhanced tumoricidal activity compared with current therapies.
official_catalog_articles.title: Enhancing success rates in therapeutic antibody design through generative models

official_catalog_articles.summary: FeatureMAP improves single-cell data analysis by preserving gene-level information within the underlying manifold structure. This enables more accurate identification of transitional cell states, differentiation trajectories and key regulatory features across dynamic processes.
official_catalog_articles.title: Feature-preserving manifold approximation and projection to analyze single-cell data

official_catalog_articles.summary: DualGPT-AB is a dual-stage generative framework for therapeutic antibody design that enables multi-property optimization of CDRH3 sequences. Experiments validate designed antibodies with favorable HER2-binding affinity and tumoricidal activity.
official_catalog_articles.title: DualGPT-AB: a dual-stage generative optimization framework for therapeutic antibody design

official_catalog_articles.summary: A self-supervised foundation model, HorusEye, learns realistic noise directly from X-ray scans and enables robust tomography restoration across diverse modalities, scanners, and tasks without clean training data.
official_catalog_articles.title: Universal restoration of medical images

official_catalog_articles.summary: A benchmark to evaluate spatial alignment methods for spatial transcriptomics shows that the best approach is dataset dependent and offers actionable guidance for the future development of methods.
official_catalog_articles.title: Benchmarking alignment methods for spatial transcriptomics data

official_catalog_articles.summary: After years of progress, density functional theory is entering a period of rapid advancement, enabled by emerging generalized schemes, richer descriptors, machine learning, and the anticipated development of broader, higher-quality datasets.
official_catalog_articles.title: Progress and prospects of density functional development

official_catalog_articles.summary: Submitting an appeal regarding an editorial decision may require a significant investment of time and effort from authors. Therefore, it is important to understand what an appeal entails before making the decision on whether to appeal.
official_catalog_articles.title: To appeal or not to appeal

official_catalog_articles.summary: The authors demonstrate that the accuracy of predictions in network biology scales with larger foundation models pretrained with larger, more diverse data and that quantization enables resource-efficient predictions while preserving biological knowledge.
official_catalog_articles.title: Scaling and quantization of large-scale foundation model enables resource-efficient predictions in network biology

official_catalog_articles.summary: HorusEye is a foundation model for universal X-ray tomography restoration that learns realistic degradation directly from data. It supports imaging at substantially lower doses and reduces hardware requirements while improving expert analysis and downstream AI performance.
official_catalog_articles.title: HorusEye: a self-supervised foundation model for generalizable X-ray tomography restoration

official_catalog_articles.summary: InstructNA leverages nucleic acid large language models with HT-SELEX for de novo generation of functional nucleic acids, exhibiting high efficiency and general applicability in designing aptamers for various targets.
official_catalog_articles.title: De novo design of functional nucleic acids of aptamers

official_catalog_articles.summary: This study introduces a unified framework for brain MRI tissue segmentation and region parcellation across the lifespan, demonstrating robust and consistent performance across heterogeneous datasets using a single model.

new_articles.summary: A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.
new_articles.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
new_articles.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict chemical and material properties, and when data are scarce, data acquisition is often necessary to support these efforts. Despite the practical advantages of minimizing acquisition costs, it remains unclear which data acquisition strategies are the most efficient across diverse property prediction tasks or what principled basis underlies their relative performance. Here we survey 100 space-filling and active learning algorithms across 60 property prediction tasks, finding that cluster-based training set selection consistently outperforms active learning when choosing from a predefined candidate library, a result that runs counter to prevailing practice and is robust to the dimensionality of material representations, the choice of fixed or learned representations, and training set size. A theoretical framework grounded in Gaussian process variance establishes cluster-based selection as the principled optimum in the low-data limit, providing a unified basis for understanding training set quality across contexts. Overall, this work establishes cluster-based training set selection as a broadly effective and principled strategy for data-efficient, machine-learning-enabled materials design.

We discuss the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematical research and explore its implications for the computational science community.

On 8 September 2026, OpenAI announced that its AI agents had produced an analytical solution to one of the most prominent unsolved problems in fluid dynamics: whether the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem admits globally smooth solutions under given initial conditions and external forces. Although the claim remains controversial and has sparked substantial debate within the mathematical community1, it has raised important questions for computational scientists regarding the future role of AI in scientific discovery and the practical integration of increasingly autonomous AI systems into the research process.

In recent years, AI has increasingly contributed to solving mathematical problems. For instance, advancements such as DeepONet have demonstrated the ability of deep learning models to learn solution operators for complex differential equations, opening new avenues for computing and surrogate modeling2. new_articles.summary: The study shows that guiding AI agents with descriptions of how people make decisions in a supply-chain game helps agents reproduce collective human behavior.
new_articles.title: Cognitive grounding improves LLM simulation of collective human behavior
new_articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly stand in for human participants, yet a plausible response is not evidence of a human decision process. The gap matters most when agents interact, where locally reasonable choices compound through delays and feedback into collective outcomes. Behavioral models fit decision rules to human data; we ask whether their qualitative content alone can drive LLM agents, an approach we call cognitive grounding. Here we show, across 231 sessions of the Beer Distribution Game, a supply-chain experiment in which players’ orders amplify demand swings, that grounding moves seven LLMs toward human-calibrated behavior. Ungrounded agents reproduce the game’s instability but miss its magnitude, timing and propagation; grounding improves trajectory fit for every model and generally shifts inferred decision parameters toward the human-calibrated reference, although unevenly across roles and models. The effect holds against independent empirical data and under alternative prompting and memory designs. Cognitively grounded LLMs are therefore candidate behavioral surrogates, contingent on task-specific validation.

Abstract

Large language models (LLMs) increasingly stand in for human participants, yet a plausible response is not evidence of a human decision process. The gap matters most when agents interact, where locally reasonable choices compound through delays and feedback into collective outcomes. Behavioral models fit decision rules to human data; we ask whether their qualitative content alone can drive LLM agents, an approach we call cognitive grounding. Large language models have increasingly demonstrated strong medical abilities, while vision–language models extend these capabilities to clinical images and other multimodal data. Yet, strong performance on individual benchmarks does not automatically translate into useful clinical applications. To be deployed in healthcare, models must adapt to local settings, integrate with clinical information systems, and support complex reasoning across heterogeneous patient data. new_articles.summary: Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.
new_articles.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
new_articles.abstract: The accurate quantum chemical calculation of excited states is a challenging task, often requiring computationally demanding methods. When entire ground and excited potential energy surfaces (PESs) are desired, for instance, to predict the interaction of light excitation and structural changes, one is often forced to use cheaper computational methods at the cost of reduced accuracy. Here we introduce a method for the geometrically transferable optimization of neural network wavefunctions that leverages weight sharing and a dynamical ordering of electronic states. Our method enables the efficient prediction of ground- and excited-state PESs and their intersections at the highest accuracy, demonstrating up to two orders of magnitude cost reduction compared with single-point calculations. We validate our approach on four challenging excited-state PESs, namely, ethylene, the carbon dimer, the methylenimmonium cation and a rubredoxin active site model containing 96 electrons, illustrating the potential of transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo as a practical framework for studying electronic excitations in molecules.

new_articles.summary: This study presents a scalable, efficient framework for unconventional computing with physical neural networks. It replaces dense connections with uncoupled one-dimensional dynamics, simplifies training, improves performance and reduces resource use.
new_articles.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
new_articles.abstract: Escalating energy demands for high-performance machine learning have sparked growing interest in unconventional computing paradigms rooted in physical systems. Central to this direction is leveraging physical properties to design computing frameworks integrating strong learning capabilities, efficient training strategies and practical implementability. Here we present a simple, efficient and scalable framework aimed at achieving this, validated on an optoelectronic platform. This framework features our proposed training mechanism, state-skipping direct feedback alignment, together with our single-map architecture based on simple one-dimensional dynamics. The former eliminates the need to access the system’s intermediate states during training, substantially simplifying error backpropagation, while the latter removes complex internal interconnections. Together, they enhance training efficiency and practical feasibility. Compared with conventional deep neural networks, our approach substantially reduces computational costs and trainable parameter count while achieving comparable performance. Integrated into modern architectures, our scheme attains improved performance with an approximately 40% reduction in computational resources. Notably, our approach challenges the scaling laws of conventional counterparts, underscoring its strong scalability and practical promise.
